newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says will support NCB reforms with BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says will support NCB reforms with BOJ.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday that the ministry, together with the Bank of Japan (BOJ), will support restructuring efforts by Nippon Credit Bank.
The ministry has not, however, heard anything formally about the content of the bank's restructuring plans.
Mitsuzuka said the ministry has been telling the bank that the basic policy should be that the bank makes its own efforts to restructure its business.
"We will be informed when the bank has decided on the plan. As we said before, the ministry will cooperate with the BOJ to formally support the bank's efforts," he said.

"Nippon Credit Bank is one of the 20 key banks in Japan. It is also a key bank in the domestic and global financial markets," he said, adding that NCB's efforts at restructuring were important for the stability of the financial markets.
Mitsuzuka also reiterated the ministry's basic stance that it would do its best to ensure stability in Japan's financial system.

Banking sources said on Friday that Japanese financial authorities were considering financial support measures for NCB, in cooperation with major banks and life insurance companies, totalling 300 billion yen.
NCB said on Thursday it expected to unveil its restructuring plan in early April and banking sources said it would include selling real estate and shutting down some operations overseas.
Asked about the protection of bank debentures, Mitsuzuka said that it was important to strengthen the issuing banks' credibility by improving their financial status.
